title: Node command line tool with parseArgs and --help
when: The user wants a command line tool in Node with flags, positional arguments, a help screen and proper exit codes.
prompt:
Goal: A dependency free CLI that parses flags with util.parseArgs, explains itself with --help and behaves in scripts and pipes.
Steps:
1. Line 1 #!/usr/bin/env node; import { parseArgs } from "node:util".
2. Options with types, short aliases and defaults ({ help: { type: "boolean", short: "h" }, out: { type: "string", short: "o" } }), allowPositionals and strict true.
3. Parse inside try: on an unknown flag print the message plus "Run with --help" to stderr and set exit code 2.
4. HELP text: usage line, one line summary, each option with its default, two examples; --help prints it to stdout and exits 0.
5. Read input from a file argument, or stdin when the argument is "-" or stdin is not a TTY, so the tool works in pipes.
6. Results to stdout, diagnostics to stderr; runtime errors give exit code 1 via process.exitCode.
Quality bar:
- Output is plain and parseable; color only on a TTY without NO_COLOR.
- Help matches the real options.
- Starts fast: no heavy work before parsing.
Pitfalls:
- Hand parsing process.argv with index math.
- Errors printed to stdout, corrupting piped output.
- Exit code 0 after a failure.
Verify:
- [ ] Shebang present.
- [ ] --help prints usage and exits 0.
- [ ] Unknown flags exit with 2.
- [ ] Errors go to stderr.
Output: bin/<name>.mjs and a "bin" entry in package.json naming it.

examples.input: a CLI that converts markdown files to html with an --out flag
examples.output: bin/md2html.mjs with parseArgs, --help text, stdin support and exit codes 0, 1, 2
